video.title: I Told an AI Agent to Make Me Money. It Did.

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Brandon Doyle (David AI), who used his OpenClaw AI agent ("Zach Morris", reached via iMessage) to launch three experiments over a month. A custom bedtime-story email subscription (Dreamtales) reached about $300 MRR from ~33 customers on roughly $400 of ads. An agent-built website plus postcard plus cold-call funnel for 350 Utah home-service businesses produced a claimed ~$8K MRR from about 17-20 marketing clients. A Facebook Marketplace/eBay flipping idea was dropped. The key takeaway is that agents did the build and outreach prep, while hard-to-ignore physical postcards and human closing calls drove the results.

speakers.name: Brandon Doyle
speakers.description: Founder of David AI (getdavid.ai), AI solutions company in Provo, Utah; heavy OpenClaw user

ideas.name: Free agent-built websites + postcard + call funnel selling AI marketing packages
ideas.one_liner: An agent scraped 350 Utah home-service businesses, built a site for each, mailed QR-code postcards via Lob, and a human salesperson called to sell marketing packages.
ideas.business_model: Monthly marketing retainers; website given free with the cheapest package
ideas.customer: Small local home-service businesses (landscaping, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing) in Utah with no or poor websites
ideas.problem: Local service businesses have no or bad websites and are flooded with low-effort marketing pitches
ideas.offer: A free pre-built website (business info, reviews, click-to-call) if they sign up for AI-powered marketing services

pricing.model: Monthly retainer packages; free website bundled with the cheapest tier
pricing.notes: Most customers take the cheapest package (a few hundred dollars a month); average about $400/month across ~17-20 customers.

acquisition_channels.details: Lob API postcards with a QR code to the customer's own free site; ~$1+ each, 341 of 350 delivered, claimed ~20% scanned.

quote.text: We built you a free website. Scan the QR code to see your new site.
quote.speaker: Brandon Doyle

acquisition_channels.details: Part-time salesperson called all 350, prioritising people who scanned the QR code, pitching the cheapest package with the free site.
Leads (names, phones, emails, business info) scraped from Google Business/Maps listings across Utah.

ideas.delivery: Agent built the sites cheaply with Chinese models on test URLs; marketing services are delivered by David AI (AI-powered marketing); a human closes the deals.
unit_economics_claims: ~14 of 68 scanners closed; ~90% of closes were scanners
ideas.startup_cost: About $400 postcards plus $10-20 tokens plus sales rep time

acquisition.how: Lead scraping, site generation and postcard sending via Lob API are automated, but closing relies on human cold calls; calls to limited companies need TPS/CTPS screening.

onboarding.how: Service onboarding for marketing clients likely needs human setup; not described.

delivery.how: AI-powered marketing services are delivered by AI with routine checks; details not stated.

billing.how: Recurring subscription billing can be automated; not described.

support.how: Client communication for marketing retainers needs human involvement.

uk_applicability.notes: Postcards are legal in the UK (PECR does not cover addressed post, but UK GDPR legitimate interest and Royal Mail rules apply); sole-trader data and cold calls need TPS/CTPS screening; Lob has UK equivalents (e.g. Royal Mail-based APIs). Companies House and Google Maps data are available.

risks: Conversion data on sites vs no-site wasn't tracked
Some closes may have come from the call alone, not the postcard
Scaling risks quality of client work

tactics.name: Pre-built free site + QR postcard + warm call
steps: Scrape Google Maps/Business listings for local service businesses
Have the agent build a cheap site per business from public data (use low-cost models)
Mail a postcard via Lob API with a QR code to their site and your contact info
Track scans and have a salesperson call scanners first
Offer the site free with the cheapest marketing package

quote.text: as soon as we hear that they scanned for sure call on those like super hard
quote.speaker: Brandon Doyle

tactics.name: Stack friction-heavy touches to stand out
steps: Combine several hard-to-fake touches (custom site, physical mail, phone calls)
Avoid mass email/DM that looks like bot spam
Consider a fourth touch such as hand delivery

quote.text: if you compound your difficult things, compound your frictionful things, then you compound your wins
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Deliver product inside existing channels (email/iMessage) instead of an app
steps: Use email or messaging as the delivery vehicle
Avoid building another app people won't install

tactics.name: Founder-led video ad on Meta with open targeting
steps: Record a 15-20 second talking-to-camera ad as a parent with the same problem

tactics.name: Cut token costs for bulk generation
steps: Tell the agent to keep token cost low
Host on test URLs rather than custom domains initially

warnings.warning: Hosting hundreds of live sites on Replit would get costly.
Some closes may have come from calls alone, so postcard attribution is uncertain.

lessons.lesson: Put the product where users already are (email, iMessage) rather than building another app.

quote.text: We don't want another app. We want a problem solved.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Agents are best at building and prep; humans still close deals and drive conversion.
Doing the hard, costly thing (physical mail, personalised assets, calls) differentiates when everyone else spams email.
Giving the agent explicit cost constraints (cheap models) made 350 sites cost cents each.
A $9/month product that breaks even on ads in month one can be fine since the revenue recurs.
Run experiments with a clear tracking plan; missing attribution limited learning.
Drop low-priority experiments when others work (opportunity cost).
Founder-led, human-faced creative beat AI avatar ads.
Repeating experiments monthly and refining (e.g. SEO angle for sites that rank poorly) compounds learning.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific figures, but self-reported, unverified, a single month, and with attribution gaps (customer count ranges 17-20, closes partly from calls). The $8K MRR comes from selling the operator's own existing agency services.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Brandon sells AI services via David AI (getdavid.ai) and uses this as a showcase; Koerner promotes Beehiiv (sponsor) and his TKO community.
